# One-page summary

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_docs.py from results/*.json and data/facts.csv. Edit docs/templates/one_page_summary.md instead. -->

*Independent desk study on public information, built with AI assistance; not affiliated with or endorsed by any
authority, operator or government. Stylised model, illustrative contract terms. Author: Wenjie Luo (GitHub
LUOaini1213).*

**Question.** Who should carry ridership, cost and fare-lag risk when a rail operator is appointed, and what
changes for a long cross-border concession where the operator sets the fare?

**What is public.** Singapore's existing lines run on a framework in which the operator keeps fares and pays a
licence charge, with shortfall and profit sharing in its second version (F02, F04, F05). New lines have been let
on a service fee, with the Government keeping fare revenue (F17, F22, F26). The Cross Island Line operating
contract was {{fact:F25}} in November 2024 (F25). The RTS Link has a {{fact:F64}} first concession, operator-set
fares and service expected in {{fact:F72}} (F64, F66, F72); no fare had been announced when sources were checked.

**What the stylised model shows** ({{archetypes.json:n_sims|int}} simulations, {{archetypes.json:years|int}}
years, every option priced to the same {{archetypes.json:params.target_margin|pct0}} expected margin):

| Option | Operator loses money over the term | Authority's present value: standard deviation (S$m) | Operator keeps per extra ridership dollar |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A. Net-cost concession | {{archetypes.json:metrics.A.p_loss_cumulative|pct0}} | {{archetypes.json:metrics.A.authority_npv_sd|.0f}} | {{archetypes.json:marginal_incentives.expected.A.revenue|.2f}} |
| B. Gross-cost service fee | {{archetypes.json:metrics.B.p_loss_cumulative|pct0}} | {{archetypes.json:metrics.B.authority_npv_sd|.0f}} | {{archetypes.json:marginal_incentives.expected.B.revenue|.2f}} |
| C. Hybrid with sharing bands | {{archetypes.json:metrics.C.p_loss_cumulative|pct0}} | {{archetypes.json:metrics.C.authority_npv_sd|.0f}} | {{archetypes.json:marginal_incentives.expected.C.revenue|.2f}} |
| D. Long concession, operator-set fares | {{archetypes.json:metrics.D.p_loss_cumulative|pct0}} | {{archetypes.json:metrics.D.authority_npv_sd|.0f}} | {{archetypes.json:marginal_incentives.expected.D.revenue|.2f}} |

- Risk moves; it is not removed. The more the operator is protected, the more the authority's budget varies and
  the less the operator gains from growing ridership.
- A cap on yearly fare increases is a risk-allocation choice: covered by subsidy it falls on the authority
  (about S${{archetypes.json:headline.fare_cap_cost_authority_A|.0f}}m in the model), uncovered on the operator.
- A long term raises tail exposure: over {{archetypes.json:concession_30_years.years|int}} years the assumed
  chance of at least one pandemic-like event is {{archetypes.json:concession_30_years.p_at_least_one_pandemic|pct0}}.

**RTS Link arithmetic.** The published opening estimate, {{rts.json:inputs.opening_estimate|int}} passengers a
day (F69), is {{rts.json:opening_share_of_woodlands|pct0}} of Woodlands Checkpoint volume (F77). At an
illustrative S${{rts.json:inputs.reference_fare|.0f}} fare that is S${{rts.json:reference_revenue_m|.0f}}m a
year; an illustrative S${{rts.json:inputs.reference_cost_m|.0f}}m yearly cost would need
{{rts.json:break_even.1.by_fare.1.daily_trips|int}} trips a day. Real costs and fares are not public.

**Trade-offs, not a recommendation.** Service fees suit new lines with unknown demand but need a strong incentive
regime. Net-cost forms give commercial drive but expose the operator in downturns. Hybrids sit between and are
hard to calibrate. Long concessions with operator-set fares remove fare lag but concentrate tail risk.

**What would change this.** A ridership record; flexible costs; evidence on how demand responds to fares; the
real contract terms, none of which are public.

**Limits.** Contract terms are placeholders; costs and demand do not respond to each other; the fact base is a
snapshot of {{fact_check.json:checked_on|str}}. Full detail: [policy brief](policy_brief.md),
[fact base](fact_base.md), repository README.
